analysis.title: Something is seriously wrong with the euro
key_insights: EURUSD is breaking below 1.10, well under its 200-day moving average, and is testing a major trendline and the first serious support zone. RSI is oversold but not at the extreme readings seen earlier this autumn.
The euro keeps falling even though oil and gas prices have fallen, credit protection has eased since late October, and relative EU-US economic surprises have started to bounce.
TS Lombard argues softer oil could make the ECB less hawkish while sticky US services inflation keeps the Fed tightening, which would widen rate differentials in favour of the dollar.
TS Lombard says Brent may need to fall towards $70 before FX markets price a broader global growth recovery.

TS Lombard's dollar bull/bear indicator is at its strongest level since 2023. The bank expects more dollar strength from resilient US growth, a recovering labour market and sticky services inflation keeping the Fed more hawkish than markets anticipate.
The dollar is rising despite a tech sell-off and is overshooting the widening in US rate differentials. Deutsche Bank says foreigners are buying US equities aggressively into the weakness.

Deutsche Bank's tracker of more than 100 foreign-domiciled ETFs shows the largest two-week buying of US stocks this year. DB questions whether that buying and widening rate differentials can both continue if market turmoil persists.

Bearish euro positioning is already substantial. TS Lombard's tactical FX positioning indicator is around -1.0 and the bank keeps its negative EURUSD view. The Market Ear flags that crowded positioning matters as EURUSD nears major support with RSI oversold.
